minutes.headline: Assessors will interview seven Town Assessor applicants by Zoom and want the outside firm kept on past June 30.
minutes.summary: The Board of Assessors met remotely to plan how to screen seven applicants for Town Assessor. They agreed one member would lead screening, with questions compiled by May 18 and interviews around May 26-28. They also discussed keeping the current contract assessing firm for an interim period or using Tyler for help, and agreed to call the state DOR and another town about the conversion approval. Only the adjournment was moved.

budget_items.what_was_said: The board noted the RFP was written for one year to cover the transition. The contractor did not respond and is not planning to.

budget_items.topic: Tyler per diem help with interim adjustments
budget_items.what_was_said: A member suggested Tyler could assist on a per diem basis, paying only for work needed.

budget_items.topic: Extending the current contractor monthly past June 30
budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager preferred keeping the current contractor on a monthly rate for continuity. The contract ends June 30 and the firm said it would provide the same level of services.

what_happened.line: The Board of Assessors met by Zoom and agreed the chair will lead screening of seven applicants for Town Assessor, with a schedule set with two other members.
Interview questions are due to the compiling member by May 18, with Zoom interviews of about an hour each tentatively set for May 26 through 28.
The board discussed keeping the current contract assessing firm on a monthly basis past June 30; the town manager preferred that for continuity.
One member will call another town about its conversion, and another will call the state DOR Bureau of Local Assessment chief about approval.
No votes were taken on these items; the only motion was to adjourn.

why_it_matters: Who is hired as Town Assessor, and whether an outside firm stays on after June 30, shapes how property valuations are set and who is paid to do that work, which feeds into tax bills.
The one-year assessing services request drew no response from the current contractor, so the interim arrangement and any added per diem help remain unsettled costs in the town budget, mostly taxes.
